Testimony in support:
LD 1447, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite
Reimbursement of All Vendors"
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
April 14th, 2025
Senator lngwerson, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Laura Harper, l live in Hallowell and I'm a Senior
Associate at Moose Ridge Associates. l'm here today to provide testimony on behalf of my client, Maine Family Planning, in support of LD 1447, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite Reimbursement of All Vendors."
Maine Family Planning provides comprehensive sexual and reproductive health care to teens and adults at 19 locations statewide. Our mission is to ensure that all people have access to high-quality, culturally relevant and affordable sexual and reproductive health care services, comprehensive sexual health education, and the right to control their sexual and reproductive lives.
in addition to the sexual and reproductive health services you would assume MFP provides, we
offer expanded services for pregnant women, new moms, and their families in Hancock and
Washington counties. We are the WIC provider for Downeast Maine with offices in Calais, Ellsworth
and Machias. As you know, WIC works to maintain the health of women, infants and children up to
age five by providing information on eating well and vouchers for healthy foods.
in Hancock county we also operate Maine Families which provides in-home parenting information
while developing caring, supportive relationships with parents. Our Maine Families program provides resources for families around pregnancy, nutrition, baby and child health care, breastfeeding/formula feeding, immunizations, child growth and development, discipline, toilet
training, and child and household safety. We also operate a monthly play group in Ellsworth for
families in the program with children up to three years old.
Both our WIC and Maine Families offices are reporting that many of the families served are struggling to find providers who take MaineCare because of the slow and low reimbursement rates.
In these rural counties where there is already a shortage of healthcare clinicians, delays in reimbursements for MaineCare services exacerbates deferred prevention, treatment and care in a population already strained by low-wages, transportation challenges, and other socio-economic
barriers. indeed, 47% of MFP patients in 2024 were covered by some type of Mainecare, either full
or the limited family planning benefit. Timely payments to MaineCare providers are crucial for us at
MFP and the families we serve.
For these reasons, Maine Family Planning urges you to vote "ought to pass" on LD 1447. Thank
you for your time today and l'm happy to try and answer any questions.

Senator Ingwersen, Chair Representative Meyer, Chair Members, Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services 100 State House Station Augusta, ME 04333-0100
Re: LD 1447 - Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite Reimbursement of All Vendors
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition of LD 1447, Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite Reimbursement of All Vendors.
This resolve requires the Department of Health and Human Services (the "Department") to amend its rules in Chapter 101: MaineCare Benefits Manual to require the Department to reimburse at least 75% of a submitted claim for services rendered within 90 days of receipt. The title of Section 1 addresses the receipt of cost reports, while the proposed language addresses submitted claims; as these filings are distinct and separate, the Department requests clarity as to the actual intent of the bill. Currently, the Department understands the intent of LD 1447 to be that the Department must pay a percentage of the amount submitted on any individual claim within a certain time period; if this is not the intent, the language needs to be clarified.
MaineCare already must comply with federal prompt pay requirements, which mandate 90% of clean claims be paid within 30 days of receipt and 99% of clean claims be paid within 90 days of receipt (a clean claim is one that comes into the claims processing system with all the basic information needed to process the claim.) Failure to pay claims according to these requirements could result in loss of federal funds. Prompt pay requirements, which apply to the entirety of a claim, are therefore more strict than what this bill is proposing.
This bill refers to a "submitted claim," implying that the Department must pay 75% of the amount that a provider charges the Department. Claims go through a complicated adjudication process, with different payment methodologies applied to different types of providers and services. The eventual amount paid is not always the entirety or a specific percentage of the charge amount; MaineCare may also deny part or all of a claim for various reasons. It would violate MaineCare policy to ignore the claims adjudication process and default to paying 75% of the amount on a submitted claim.
Additionally, the Department's claims processing system is not configured to pay a percentage of the amount eventually owed on any individual claim: each line on a claim (each submitted charge) must have a status of paid, denied, or pending, where pending indicates further information or review is needed. Implementing the bill as drafted would require a manual process for pending, reporting, tracking, calculating, paying, and subsequently adjusting claims; this is not practical or feasible and does not align with federal prompt pay or reporting requirements. Should this bill move forward, additional staff will be

required to facilitate burdensome manual claims processing, although without more clarity on the intent of the bill, it is not possible to estimate the number of new staff needed.
If the intent of the bill is indeed to address cost reports as written in the title of section 1, the net fiscal impact would be $34,456,903 in SFY 2025 and approximately $90,000-$96,000 for subsequent years.
Federal prompt pay requirements already mandate swifter payments to providers than what is proposed in this LD. The Department encourages the committee to support the Department's current practices as the proposed changes in LD 1447 would not be in the best interest of MaineCare enrolled providers, MaineCare members, or the Department. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,
Michelle Probert Director Office of MaineCare Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services

LD 1447, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services
to Expedite Reimbursement of All Vendors"
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
April 14, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services:
I am Trey Stewart; and I represent Senate District 2, which includes several communities in
Penobscot and Aroostook Counties. I am here to present LD 1447, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite Reimbursement of All Vendors."
Those of you who sat on this panel during the 131" Legislature may recall a bill I sponsored, LD
1474, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Expedite
Reimbursement of Nursing Facilities," which was finally passed and signed by the Governor in 2023. The proposal before you today is quite similar -- exact in its intention but more encompassing in that it requires the Department to expedite reimbursement to all vendors.
I would be willing to bet that all of you have heard from constituents and/or facilities that are
waiting on Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) reimbursement payments -- foster
families, dental practices, hospitals, long-term care facilities and, yes, nursing facilities. Coupled
with a workforce shortage, caregiving services who support our most vulnerable friends and
neighbors needlessly grapple with juggling finances because their MaineCare reimbursements are not coming in for months and sometimes years amounting to, in some cases, hundreds of thousands -- even millions of dollars.
It's really very simple. Pay your bills. This measure would require the Department to reimburse
at least 75% of a submitted claim within 90 days of receipt. Three months' time is not
unreasonable for payment to be made. Facilities have, in some cases, been stretched to the brink under the financial strain of staying afloat. They have used up their lines of credit, which is a shame they have to resort to this just because the state is not fulfilling their financial obligations.
To be clear, this is not a bailout for MaineCare. This irresponsible bureaucratic nightmare has been going on for years -- long before the current gap in MaineCare. During the previous administration the hospitals were paid and made whole and a mechanism was put in place to
